title: A torticollis visit and a hip clunk
objective: Screen infant hips with the Ortolani and Barlow tests and watch for limited abduction, uneven gluteal folds and leg-length difference; breech position is the biggest risk factor for hip dysplasia
secondaryObjectives: Know infant hip dysplasia management may include an abduction splint such as the Pavlik harness, set by the orthopedic surgeon, and that screening aims to diagnose before 6 months

brief.situation: 09:00 in an outpatient pediatric clinic. You are the physical therapist. Ana, 7 weeks old, was referred for right torticollis. She was born breech by cesarean. Her newborn hip check was recorded as 'normal'.
handover: Her mother swaddles her 'tight like a burrito, legs straight' to help her sleep.
Clinic policy: infants seen for torticollis get a hip screen; a positive screen goes to pediatric orthopedics for ultrasound the same week, and the pediatrician is told.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each check takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: A breech-born infant with torticollis has a positive left Ortolani, limited abduction, uneven folds and a leg-length difference: probable developmental dysplasia of the hip.
parts.modelAnswer: Her left hip clunks back in on Ortolani, abduction is limited, the folds are uneven and the knee sits low. She was breech. That's probably hip dysplasia.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Refers to pediatric orthopedics for ultrasound this week (a Pavlik harness works best before 6 months), tells the pediatrician, teaches hip-healthy swaddling and treats the torticollis.
parts.modelAnswer: Refer her to pediatric orthopedics this week, tell the pediatrician, teach hip-healthy swaddling, and keep treating the neck.

scoring.modelReasoning: Breech position is the biggest risk factor for hip dysplasia, and torticollis often travels with it. Screen with Barlow and Ortolani and look for limited abduction, uneven gluteal folds and a leg-length difference. A positive screen goes to pediatric orthopedics; management may include an abduction splint such as the Pavlik harness, and screening aims to diagnose before 6 months.
